Full pre-registration sweep (cross-model independent audit, auditor = claude-code, cycle 1): READY (Ready + Clean). 0 BLOCKING, 0 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 1 SUGGESTION. By issue type: 0 factual, 0 structural, 1 scope-related (suggestion only). Source fetch was ENABLED; both the cited Britannica source and a Wikipedia validation source were fetched successfully.

=== SOURCE GROUNDING (cited source) ===
Cited source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/worlds-largest-islands-2228256 (role: universe + ranking + value; single source; this IS the staged ground-truth set). RISK #1 (source-name consistency) RESOLVED: the cited URL is genuinely Encyclopaedia Britannica, matching the id/title 'britannica'. No provenance mismatch. Britannica presents the '10 largest islands' block followed by 'the next 15 largest islands' block (25 entries total); the instance correctly takes the first 20.

=== ROW-LEVEL CORRECTNESS (all 20 rows verified verbatim vs Britannica) ===
Every row matches the cited Britannica page exactly on rank, island name, area (sq km), and region text:
  1 Greenland 2166086 (North Atlantic Ocean and Arctic Ocean) - MATCH
  2 New Guinea 821400 (Malay Archipelago, western Pacific Ocean) - MATCH
  3 Borneo 755000 - MATCH
  4 Madagascar 591896 - MATCH
  5 Baffin Island 507451 - MATCH
  6 Sumatra 480793 - MATCH
  7 Honshu 227898 - MATCH
  8 Victoria Island 217291 - MATCH
  9 Great Britain 209331 - MATCH
  10 Ellesmere Island 196236 - MATCH
  11 Sulawesi 188522 (Britannica prints 'Sulawesi/Celebes'; see SUGGESTION S1) - MATCH (area/rank/region)
  12 South Island 152229 - MATCH
  13 Java 127570 - MATCH
  14 North Island 116219 - MATCH
  15 Newfoundland 108860 - MATCH
  16 Luzon 104688 - MATCH
  17 Cuba 104339 - MATCH
  18 Iceland 103000 - MATCH
  19 Mindanao 94630 - MATCH
  20 Ireland 84421 - MATCH
No missing, incorrect, duplicate, or unsupported rows. (factual: 0 issues)

=== RANKING / TOP-K CORRECTNESS (RISK #2) ===
- Greenland is #1. CORRECT.
- Australia is EXCLUDED. CORRECT - Britannica explicitly treats continents/mainlands as non-islands; Australia does not appear in its island list.
- #18-22 cutoff boundary verified against Britannica's own ordering: #18 Iceland (103,000), #19 Mindanao (94,630), #20 Ireland (84,421) are the staged cutoff; Britannica's #21 Hokkaido (77,978) and #22 Sakhalin (76,400) are correctly EXCLUDED. The #20 cutoff at Ireland matches the cited source exactly. CORRECT.
- Locator for all of the above: Britannica article body, '10 largest islands' list (positions 1-10) and 'next 15 largest islands' list (positions 11-25).

=== AREA VALUES + UNITS (RISK #3) ===
All 20 area values are byte-for-byte the Britannica sq-km figures with commas/unit words stripped to bare integers (e.g. Greenland 2,166,086 -> 2166086). Column header is 'Area (sq km)'; unit is consistent km2 across ALL 20 rows. No sq-mi contamination. CORRECT. (column_types: Area=numeric matches.)

=== source_count=1 (RISK #4) ===
VERIFIED. The single Britannica source defines the full ranked top-20 AND every area value. No supplemental rows or sources were used (consistent with draft _extraction_notes and curation proposed_supplements=[]). source_count=1 is accurate.

=== PREFLIGHT / STRUCTURAL (RISK #5) ===
- Row count: 20 (excl header). CORRECT.
- CSV header 'Rank,Island,Area (sq km),Region' == draft.columns exactly. CORRECT.
- PK = [Island]: all 20 island names unique, no duplicates. CORRECT. (PK on Island rather than Rank is a deliberate, documented choice so rank errors score as non-key cell errors.)
- Rank column: monotonic 1..20. CORRECT.
- Area: strictly descending across all 20 rows. CORRECT (consistent with ORDER BY area_sq_km DESC).
- column_types {Rank: rank, Island: key, Area (sq km): numeric, Region: text}: all consistent with the data. CORRECT.
No structural issues. (structural: 0 issues)

=== WIKI-FAMILY SOURCE DISCOVERY PASS (validation, NOT ground truth) ===
Fetched https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_by_area as a validation/challenge source. Findings:
- Wikipedia reports DIFFERENT area values (Greenland 2,130,800 vs Britannica 2,166,086; New Guinea 785,753 vs 821,400; Sumatra 443,065 vs 480,793; etc.) and a DIFFERENT order near the cutoff: Wikipedia ranks Luzon #15 / Newfoundland #16 (swapped vs Britannica's Newfoundland #15 / Luzon #16) and Great Britain #8 vs Britannica #9.
- This is NOT a missing-source defect. It CONFIRMS that source identity is load-bearing for this ranking and that the instance correctly cites Britannica and honestly declares claim_type=source_defined. Wikipedia is an alternative universe, not a missing piece of the Britannica-defined universe. No Wikipedia/Wikidata/sibling/redirect source materially changes the staged Britannica-defined row universe, ranking rule, or partition boundary.
- Conclusion: no missing Wiki-family source. (No BLOCKING or HYGIENE finding from discovery.)

=== METADATA / REGISTRATION ===
- query_category=top_k: valid vocab (categories.txt: 'ORDER BY col DESC LIMIT K'). Correct fit.
- operation_type=projection: valid vocab (curation_protocol.md 'projection - single-source multi-column SELECT, no filter'; UI selectbox lists projection). The draft/curation honestly note projection is the closest UI-supported coarse op and top-k semantics are carried by query_category + the ORDER BY/LIMIT db_analog. Policy-faithful, not a violation.
- claim_type=source_defined: ACCURATE - verified that areas and some rank boundaries vary across references, so the claim should be source-anchored rather than exhaustive/consensus. Honest.
- domain=Geography/Islands: Geography is a valid Family in domain_taxonomy.md; Islands is a sound Subdomain under the Geography/* convention. OK.
- temporal_sensitivity=low / temporal_note: appropriate (stable geographic facts; note correctly flags cross-reference area variation). gt_construction=web_search_britannica matches the source. source_urls[0] role = universe+ranking+value, all carried by the one Britannica page. All metadata correct.

=== LLM-KNOWABLE FIT + BENCHMARK VALUE ===
Good parametric-knowledge target: a stable, broadly knowable geography ranking that fills the previously empty top_k category. The Britannica-vs-Wikipedia divergence makes it a useful source-fidelity probe (does a model reproduce the CITED source's ranking, not a blended/popular one?). Helps the benchmark's structured-extraction + source-grounding story.

=== FINDINGS (separated by severity) ===
BLOCKING: none.
NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE: none.
SUGGESTION:
  S1 (scope-related, SUGGESTION): Britannica's display name for rank 11 is 'Sulawesi/Celebes'; the CSV uses 'Sulawesi'. This is exactly the normalization the curation.json declares (alternate names omitted unless Britannica uses them as the main form) and 'Sulawesi' is the standard primary form, so no change is required. A curator could optionally record 'Celebes' as an accepted alias in normalization_decisions for full provenance. Locator: Britannica 'next 15 largest islands' list, position 11. Source: cited ground-truth source.

=== VERDICT ===
READY (Ready + Clean). The instance is source-grounded (all 20 cells verbatim from the cited Britannica page), structurally clean (PK unique, header==columns, ranks 1..20, area strictly descending, column_types consistent), correctly scoped (source_defined, source_count=1, Australia excluded, Greenland #1, #20 cutoff at Ireland matches Britannica), and metadata-correct. The open_question in curation.json (whether to require cross-source consensus) is answered by current policy: source_defined with an honest, non-Britannica-naming title is acceptable and properly declared, so it is NOT a blocker - only an optional stronger-source upgrade. Recommend registration. No fixes required (one optional alias-recording suggestion). Audit is append-only; no canonical artifact was modified.
